questions.stem: What is the electronic configuration of sodium (atomic number 11)?
questions.explanation: Sodium has 11 electrons. The first shell holds 2, the second holds 8, and the third holds 1, giving the electronic configuration 2,8,1.

questions.stem: An element has the electronic configuration 2,8,7. In which group and period is it located?
questions.explanation: The element has 3 electron shells, so it is in Period 3. It has 7 electrons in its outer shell, so it is in Group 7. This element is chlorine.

questions.stem: What is the maximum number of electrons that can be held in the first electron shell?
questions.explanation: The first electron shell (closest to the nucleus) can hold a maximum of 2 electrons. The second and third shells can hold up to 8 electrons each.

questions.stem: Why does potassium (2,8,8,1) react similarly to sodium (2,8,1)?

options.text: They have the same number of electron shells
They have the same number of protons
They both have 1 electron in their outer shell
They have the same atomic mass

questions.explanation: Both potassium and sodium have 1 electron in their outer shell. Since chemical properties are determined by outer shell electrons, they react in similar ways (both are in Group 1).

questions.stem: An element in Group 0 has a full outer shell of electrons. What does this mean for its reactivity?

options.text: It is unreactive (inert) because it has a stable electronic configuration
It is a metal that reacts with water

questions.explanation: Group 0 elements (noble gases) have full outer electron shells, giving them a very stable electronic configuration. They have no tendency to gain, lose, or share electrons, making them unreactive.

questions.stem: What is the electronic configuration of calcium (atomic number 20)?
questions.explanation: Calcium has 20 electrons: 2 in the first shell, 8 in the second, 8 in the third, and 2 in the fourth, giving 2,8,8,2.

questions.stem: An element has 6 electrons in its outer shell and is in Period 2. What is the element?
questions.explanation: Period 2 with 6 outer electrons means the configuration is 2,6. This gives a total of 8 electrons, which is oxygen (atomic number 8).
